about: Every check the Landing pages module runs, in the masterclass order (clarity, copy, offer, proof, friction), plus truth and mobile. applies: 'page' is a page built in the app, 'url' is a page captured from a link. level is what a failure is: 'fail' blocks nothing but is shown in red; 'warn' is advice. Each check is code keyed by its id in src/lib/landing/checks.ts; this file holds the words. ice: impact, confidence and ease out of 10, for ranking fixes.

areas.label: Clarity and hierarchy
areas.question: Can a stranger understand it at once, above the fold, on a phone?

areas.label: Copy
areas.question: Does it remove doubt and speak to the actual desire?

areas.label: Offer
areas.question: Is the thing on offer worth converting on?

areas.label: Proof
areas.question: Do they believe the claim and the mechanism?

areas.label: Friction
areas.question: Is anything physically in the way of buying?

areas.label: Truth
areas.question: Is every fact on the page one the brand can stand behind?

checks.label: Above the fold says what it is, as an outcome
checks.good: The headline states the outcome for the buyer, not the product's name or its format
checks.fix: Rewrite the headline as dream outcome + benefit with a timeframe + mechanism (copy-formulas.md)

checks.label: Above the fold says why this one
checks.good: A sub-line names the mechanism or the one-of-one difference
checks.fix: Add a sub-headline: the pain, the unique mechanism, the benefit (40 words at most)

checks.label: Above the fold gives a reason to buy now
checks.good: A real reason today, from the brand's facts: a gift, a bundle saving or the price per day for a product bought again; when it arrives, free returns or instalments for a product bought once
checks.fix: Put the offer, the per-day price, or the delivery and returns line beside the price. Never invent urgency

checks.label: Above the fold gives a reason to trust
checks.good: The brand's stated rating and review count, a customer's words, or a warranty, right under the headline
checks.fix: Add the brand's own rating and count under the title, or 1 customer quote that proves the promise. Never a default score

checks.label: 1 primary call to action in the first screen
checks.good: 1 button that stands out
checks.fix: Keep 1 primary button above the fold; make the rest links

checks.label: Price visible without scrolling (product page)
checks.good: Price, and any saving in money, in the first screen
checks.fix: Move the price and the button above the fold on a phone

checks.label: Page type fits the buyer's awareness
checks.good: Advertorial for unaware and problem aware; listicle for solution aware; product page for product aware and ready
checks.fix: Change the page type, or the buyer it is for

checks.label: Every image slot has a picture
checks.good: Each slot holds a real photo of the product or a customer
checks.fix: Add product photos on the Brand brain screen, or make the image in Creative Studio (product page images, the bucket named on the slot)

checks.label: The hero carries the ad's promise
checks.good: The headline or sub-headline repeats the ad's main words; the first buying option is the ad's offer and the first image shows the same product
checks.fix: Put the ad's headline words in the hero; same buyer, same angle, same offer, same picture

checks.label: 1 angle, not every benefit
checks.good: 6 benefits or fewer, all on the page's 1 angle
checks.fix: Cut benefits that belong to another buyer's page

checks.label: Headings pass the so-what test
checks.good: Section headings say what the buyer gets
checks.fix: Lead with the outcome and justify with the feature

checks.label: Table stakes are not headlines
checks.good: Free shipping, fast delivery and great service stay small
checks.fix: Move table stakes into small print; headline what is unique

checks.label: FAQ answers reasons not to buy
checks.good: 3 or more questions, each an objection from research
checks.fix: Replace generic questions (shipping policy, brand story) with the top objections in the buyer's words. Returns, delivery and fit count when asked as the buyer's worry

checks.label: An offer worth converting on
checks.good: A bundle, routine, gift or subscription saving shown in money; for a product bought once, the price with what is in the box, delivery, returns and warranty
checks.fix: Build an offer in the Offers module and put it on the page

checks.label: Not a lazy discount
checks.good: Value added, not price cut; any discount under 30%
checks.fix: Reframe the offer: bundle, gift with purchase, routine

checks.label: Savings stated in money
checks.good: A saving is shown as an amount, not only a percent
checks.fix: Show 'Save $14' beside the percent

checks.label: Customer proof on the page
checks.good: 3 or more customer quotes
checks.fix: Import reviews in Sources; the builder uses their words

checks.label: Proof matches the promise
checks.good: At least 1 quote is about the page's promise
checks.fix: Pick reviews that prove the headline's claim
checks.source: Masterclass: proof must match the claim

checks.label: Every quote is a real customer's words
checks.good: Each quote is found in the research, or was entered by a person
checks.fix: Remove quotes that are not in the research

checks.label: Risk reversal under the button
checks.good: The guarantee, or the returns window and warranty, sits under the main button
checks.fix: Put the guarantee, or the returns window and warranty, in 1 line under the button

checks.label: A button follows the visitor on mobile
checks.good: A sticky add to cart after the hero scrolls away
checks.fix: Turn on the sticky bar

checks.label: No pop-up on arrival
checks.good: Nothing covers the page in the first seconds
checks.fix: Trigger pop-ups on exit intent or scroll depth

checks.label: Every number is one the brand states
checks.good: Prices, timeframes, counts and figures all appear in the brand brain
checks.fix: Remove or correct the number, or add it to the brand brain with its source

checks.label: No forbidden claims
checks.good: None of the brand's forbidden claims
checks.fix: Remove the claim

checks.label: No em dashes
checks.good: Commas, 'and' or '&' instead
checks.fix: Replace each dash

checks.label: No invented urgency
checks.good: Any deadline or stock line is true
checks.fix: Remove countdowns and stock lines that are not wired to real numbers

checks.label: Distinct supported reasons
checks.good: The page uses only distinct supported reasons answering the selected buyer task; section count follows evidence
checks.fix: Remove unsupported or redundant reasons; resolve the material buying objections first

checks.label: Proof placed where doubt peaks
checks.good: A real customer's words sit right after reasons 2 and 4, the reasons most likely to trigger "sure, but does it work"
checks.fix: Move a quote to reason 2 and one to reason 4; keep the review block for the end

checks.label: The price appears once, at the end
checks.good: No price before the buy box; the case is made first, then the buy box asks which plan
checks.fix: Take every price out of the hero, the lede, the problem and the reasons

checks.label: The lede does not name the product
checks.good: The first 2 paragraphs describe her situation so precisely that she assumes it has been solved; the product enters at reason 1
checks.fix: Take the brand and product names out of the opening paragraphs

checks.label: Headline of 8 to 14 words naming the audience
checks.good: The headline follows 1 of the 4 formulas: 8 to 14 words, names the audience and the problem, not the feature, and reads on a day she is not shopping
checks.fix: Rewrite under a formula: name who it is for and what it fixes, in 8 to 14 words

checks.label: 6 to 8 real questions before the offer
checks.good: The FAQ holds 6 to 8 questions buyers actually ask before buying, answered plainly, placed after the reasons and before the offer
checks.fix: Add the questions support is tired of answering; cut the ones nobody asks
